structure.heading: 2026 Headcount Forecast by Function and Demand Drivers
text_content: **2026 Headcount Forecast by Function and Demand Drivers**

The workforce plan projects total planned headcount increasing from 1,240 (Dec 2025) to 1,360 (Dec 2026), a net +120 FTE, representing a 9.7% year-over-year expansion focused on growth and reliability. This increment reflects consolidated demand drivers: product feature delivery timelines, infrastructure scalability, and customer acquisition goals tied to FY2026 revenue targets. Budgeted increases are phased across the year to align with quarterly milestone releases and capacity-to-demand constraints; hiring profiles will prioritize mid- to senior-level contributors where time-to-impact is critical and early hires offset outsourced vendor costs.
CD are budgeted to improve developer efficiency and lower long-term marginal hiring needs.

Sales capacity and go-to-market demand materially affect sales and customer-facing headcount: the Sales capacity plan assumes 12.5 quota-carrying reps per $10M ARR, with ARR rising from $120M (FY2025) to $150M (FY2026). Applying that ratio yields an implied increase in quota-carrying headcount from 150 reps (12 x 12.5) to 187.5 (~188 reps) to support the $30M ARR expansion; incremental non-quota roles (SDRs, sales ops, enablement) are sized proportionally. Ramp timing, average ramp-to-quota (months), and churn assumptions will determine the phasing of hires across Q1–Q4 2026.

structure.heading: Skill Gap Assessment and Talent Acquisition Strategy (Internal Mobility vs External Hiring)
text_content: **Skill Gap Assessment and Talent Acquisition Strategy (Internal Mobility vs External Hiring)**

Critical 2026 shortfalls are concentrated in data, security, and product leadership: 35 Data Engineers, 20 Cybersecurity Analysts, and 15 Product Managers. These gaps raise measurable delivery and risk exposure across Engineering, IT Security, and Product, increasing projected roadmap slippage and external contractor spend if unaddressed. The analysis relies on the 2026 Headcount Forecast by Function and Demand Drivers and prioritizes targeted development and hiring interventions in 2026.

We recommend a 55% internal mobility and 45% external hiring fill mix: 66 of 120 roles to be filled via internal moves and 54 of 120 via external recruitment. This balance leverages HR Talent Acquisition, Learning & Development, and line managers to reduce onboarding time, preserve institutional knowledge, and improve retention while reserving external channels for highly specialized roles and immediate capacity needs and scalability.

The external hiring plan targets a median time‑to‑fill of 52 days for Engineering and 38 days for Customer Support in 2026. To meet these targets Talent Acquisition will execute prioritized sourcing: employer branding campaigns, targeted sourcing via LinkedIn and niche job boards, university partnerships, managed service providers, and contract‑to‑hire pipelines. Metrics (time‑to‑fill, offer acceptance, quality of hire) will be tracked and reported to HR leadership.
